sn35.233:1.1: On one occasion the Venerable Ānanda and the Venerable Kāmabhū were dwelling at Kosambī in Ghosita’s Park.
sn35.233:1.2: Then, in the evening, the Venerable Kāmabhū emerged from seclusion and approached the Venerable Ānanda. He exchanged greetings with the Venerable Ānanda and,
sn35.233:1.3: when they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side and said to him:
sn35.233:2.1: “How is it, friend Ānanda, is the eye the fetter of forms or are forms the fetter of the eye?…
sn35.233:2.3: Is the mind the fetter of mental phenomena or are mental phenomena the fetter of the mind?”
sn35.233:3.1: “Friend Kāmabhū, the eye is not the fetter of forms nor are forms the fetter of the eye …
sn35.233:3.4: The mind is not the fetter of mental phenomena nor are mental phenomena the fetter of the mind,
sn35.233:3.5: but rather the desire and lust that arise there in dependence on both: that is the fetter there.
sn35.233:4.1: “Suppose, friend, a black ox and a white ox were yoked together by a single harness or yoke.
sn35.233:4.2: Would one be speaking rightly if one were to say:
sn35.233:4.3: ‘The black ox is the fetter of the white ox; the white ox is the fetter of the black ox’?”
sn35.233:4.5: The black ox is not the fetter of the white ox nor is the white ox the fetter of the black ox,
sn35.233:4.6: but rather the single harness or yoke by which the two are yoked together: that is the fetter there.”
sn35.233:4.7: “So too, friend, the eye is not the fetter of forms …
sn35.233:4.9: nor are mental phenomena the fetter of the mind,
sn35.233:4.10: but rather the desire and lust that arise there in dependence on both: that is the fetter there.”
